meet.title: Meet the companies
meet.intro: Four made-up companies will pitch you. Which stories hold up?
meet.headline: They say
tips: A headline is chosen to impress. Cash, customers and debt show what is really going on.
Each quarter one company pitches. Ask two questions to see its real numbers.
Tap any company on the board to study it. Your Judgement score updates after every decision.

why.title: Why

event.raised: It raised money because its cash was running low.
event.downRound: It sold new shares at a much lower price (a down-round): a sign of trouble.
event.failed: It ran out of cash and shut down.
event.restated: It cut its user numbers: they were not real customers.
event.layoffNews: It laid off staff, an early sign that business is slowing.

why.profitUp: Profit rose from ₹{{a}} lakh to ₹{{b}} lakh.
why.profitDown: Profit fell from ₹{{a}} lakh to ₹{{b}} lakh.
why.lossGrew: The loss grew from ₹{{a}} lakh to ₹{{b}} lakh.
why.lossShrank: The loss shrank from ₹{{a}} lakh to ₹{{b}} lakh.
why.excitement: The price rose though the numbers got worse: excitement, not earnings.
why.runwayShort: At this pace its cash lasts only about {{n}} more months.
why.ceoSold: The CEO sold shares this quarter.
why.steady: Nothing big changed. Small moves are normal noise.

stats.tagLegend: Early warning numbers move before the results do. Looks-back numbers report what already happened. Easy-to-inflate numbers look good and tell you little.
stats.locked: Not asked yet. Ask the founder at a pitch to see this.

price.name: Share price
price.explain: What one share costs now. Prices move for market reasons as well as company reasons.

valuation.name: Years of profit in the price
valuation.explain: How many years of today's profit the whole price equals. Low can mean a bargain or a shrinking business.

revenue.name: Revenue
revenue.explain: Money the company takes in. It shows speed, not whether the company can survive.

profit.name: Profit or loss
profit.explain: What is left after every cost. Above the line is profit, below it is a loss.

runway.name: Cash runway
runway.explain: How many months the company can pay its bills before the cash runs out.

debt.name: Debt
debt.explain: What it owes. Interest cover (profit divided by interest) of 3 or more is comfortable; near 1 is dangerous.

customers.name: Paying customers
customers.explain: Paying customers against everyone who signed up. A big gap means the headline number is inflated.

retention.name: Customers who stay
retention.explain: Out of 100 customers, how many are still there next quarter. High means growth is cheaper and steadier.

net.name: Net new customers
net.explain: New customers minus lost customers. Growth is both.

people.name: Employees
people.explain: Headcount. Layoffs are an early warning, long before profit drops.

ceo.name: CEO share trades
ceo.explain: Did the CEO sell or buy shares? Insiders know the company best.
ceo.sold: Sold shares {{n}} of the last 3 quarters

dossier.unmet: Not met yet. It pitches in a coming quarter.
dossier.passed: You passed on it. You only see the numbers you asked for.
dossier.noNews: No news about this company yet.
